text:
Micah: Heads-up — product asked for a trace-derived SLO for the /generate route. They want a single latency SLO and an error budget that ties into our rollouts UX. Thinking through feasibility with current OTEL pipeline and storage costs.
Anya: +1. We need to decide: do we calculate SLOs from raw spans (heavy) or derived metrics (lighter)?
Devin: my vote is derived metrics stored in metrics backend. We can emit histogram buckets from trace processor -> Prom/OTel metrics exporter. Less storage, easier dashboards.
Sasha: derived metrics are fine for 95th/99th but we lose per-request trace context for debugging. For rollouts we need traces to sample exceptions and tails.
Micah: good point. Maybe hybrid: aggregated histograms for SLOs and a small sample of full traces for error budget burn analysis.
Lenore: how small? product wants 90d retention for SLO numbers and 7d for full traces. If we keep 1% of traces we still blow storage for pro tier customers.
Anya: we can do tail-based sampling: keep more of slow/error traces and low sample for fast ones. OTEL Collector has tail sampling that inspects attributes and latency.
Devin: tail-based sampling plus attribute-based routing to mark hotpaths would help. Example rule: keep 100% of spans where root.duration_ms > 300 OR status.code != OK. Everything else sample at 0.1%
Sasha: That works but tail sampling is stateful and can be expensive on the collector side. We should consider doing it in the ingest layer (a small node pool) not on every collector.
Micah: ops-bot, can you show recent ingest CPU for otel-collector pool?
ops-bot: Current otel-collector pool (ingest-01..03): avg CPU 45%, peak 78% during release window. Memory avg 2.1GB.
Lenore: so headroom exists but we should cap complexity. Also think about attribution keys — service, route, model_variant, customer_tier. Those need to be preserved for policy evaluation and dashboard grouping.
Anya: Agree. And for SLO computation we need consistent buckets. Proposal: exporter writes Prom histograms with these labels: service, route, model_variant, tier, bucket (le/50, le/100, le/200, le/500, le+). Keep 90d in Prom long-term storage (remote_write to long-term TSDB). Full traces: 7d in ClickHouse object store with cheaper compression.
Devin: ClickHouse as trace store + metrics in Thanos? That lines up with cost goals. But querying p99 from histograms -> Prom is standard, dashboard panels will be cheap.
Sasha: We also need to surface 'error budget burn' as a single alerting metric. Derived metric: budget_burn = (window_error_rate / SLO_target) - 1 -> we can store budget_burn gauge per-route.
Micah: UX question: the rollout page needs to show live SLO, burn, and a link to sample traces filtered to the rollout tag. How can backend provide quick links?
Anya: We can add a route-level label on spans: rollout_id. In dashboards a link to trace-search with query `rollout_id=xyz & duration>100` will show the small set we kept.
Lenore: careful: we must avoid leaking rollout IDs for customer privacy. Rollout tags should be internal-only and scrubbed for public logs.
Devin: implementation sketch: OTEL pipeline -> processor that adds rollout_id when request header present; exporter sends histograms to remote_write and full traces to ClickHouse using gzip+lz4. Sampling processor does tail+rate rules.
Sasha: Can we show a brief config example in the thread so infra can estimate cost?
Micah: yes, drop a short snippet:
```
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: slow_or_error
        latency_threshold_ms: 300
        match_expression: "resource.service == 'api' && span.duration_ms > 300"
  probabilistic:
    default_sampling: 0.001
exporters:
  prometheus:
    histograms: true
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: https://traces.internal
```
Devin: looks reasonable. Suggest we add a small warm-up to keep 100% for new rollouts first 30min, then apply sampling. That prevents noisy rollouts from under-sampling.
Anya: for the SLO math, do we compute directly from histogram buckets in Prom or derive a timeseries of latency-percentile then evaluate SLO per-window?
Sasha: compute percentile from histograms (Prometheus histogram_quantile or use Thanos bucketed quantiles). Then SLO evaluation is just comparing p95/p99 to threshold. We'll report both p95 and p99 on dashboards.
Lenore: alert thresholds: page if burn > 0.5 for 10m, notify slack if > 0.2 for 1h. Also add an automated rollback hook in rollout UX if burn > 1.0 for 5m. Ops: yay or nay?
ops-bot: I can wire a webhook that triggers the rollout API when budget_burn exceeds threshold. Permissions required from product-team.
Micah: next steps: Anya and Devin to prototype pipeline + cost estimate; Sasha to draft dashboard wireframe for rollout page showing live SLO, burn, p95/p99, and sample trace link; Lenore to produce retention/cost options for 7/14/30/90d. We'll sync in 48h.
Anya: I'll start a small PoC branch with a test collector and synthetic load.
Devin: I'll model estimated object store growth for 1% vs 0.1% sampling and tail rules.
Sasha: I'll sketch the rollout panel in Figma and include the trace link behavior.
Micah: thanks all. If anyone wants to add quick wins: consider emitting an error counter per-route from the runtime — that'll make burn calculations trivial. :+1:
Lenore: noted. Also will add a compliance checkbox for export destinations.
Micah: thread wrap — will create the follow-up ticket and assign ownership after your PoC notes.
Anya: thanks, wrapping up here.
